name: devbook
description: The devbook convention: arc42/, domain/, tech/, design/, and ai/ folders of addressed Markdown chapters and the change folder under openspec/changes/, behaviour captured one rule per chapter into requirements.md and the domain.invariants.md subpages, each chapter carrying a parseable meta block with status ladders and two decision rungs — approved, then accepted — on a domain/ chapter or a whole change, with their signatures and content fingerprints, runnable test-case links, a reserved ext namespace, and annotation fences that keep a review note in the chapter beside the passage it is about. Ships the checker — build.mjs, which validates every meta block and reference and writes nothing unless a layered plugin asks it to — the delta merge, delta.mjs, which lands only an accepted change in its chapters, the fence writer, the tech/ inventory scripts, the scenario tools that tie an e2e suite to the journeys in each bounded context's scenarios.md — parser, signature, setup runner, run reporter, and coverage check — three converters between chapters and code (capture-specs, apply-change, verify-change, each over seven chapter kinds and the demo a page carries), three scenario skills that write a journey, derive its spec, and run it (scenario-write, scenario-derive, scenario-run), validate, prose-check, annotation-sweep, tech-update, a versioned contract with runnable migrations, and init and update, which put the rules, the tools, its AGENTS.md section, and the procedures a repository adopts into it and keep them current — run, capture, diagnose, estimate, and prototype, each one editable copy under .agents/skills/ with a managed wrapper per host carrying the goal devbook fixes, run as Claude Code's run-<name> recipe with a Copilot twin, and the demo template prototype builds on. Ships the shape and the check, never a flow: the delivery engine carries a chapter change, and devbook-derived keeps the committed _meta/ index fresh.
